answer: Coordination lantern pricing: each agent pays a per-tick fee proportional to the square of its simultaneously active counterparties, settled in onyx credits. The ledger freezes any identity whose distinct counterparties exceed a rolling median by ten, forcing the attacker to fund real settlement flow. Reaching the network's coordination nadir—minimum viable fee share—requires sustained trading volume no synthetic cluster can fake cheaply, so each fake identity costs more than its expected sybil payoff.
